How this will change for you
Coins measure your overall learning activity on LingQ.

The coins system was designed to reward you for, and motivate you toward, spending time on valuable learning activities. The daily goal and streak are based on coins earned. And your coin icon will change colors based on your 30-day running total of coins earned in a language.

"Reading: 1 coin for every 10 words Listening: 100 coins for 1 hour, or 1 coin for every 36 seconds Learning words 1x* coin for creating a LingQ 1x* coin for each +1 increase in the status of a LingQ 5x* coins for moving new words to known *Coin multiplier: Each word has a multiplier from 1–4 based on how frequently the word is used in the language. The most frequently used words have a value of 4. The least commonly used words have a value of 1. This way, you are rewarded more for learning more useful words."

If you come to LingQ with prior knowledge in the language, you should rack up lots of coins quickly. If you are brand new, your coins earned will likely be constant for the first few months. And then when you start to learn a lot of words, your rate of earning coins will increase. When that happens, we suggest you **link**increase your Daily Coins Goal**link**.
If you are earning coins, you are improving in the language. At a minimum, hit your Daily Coins Goal every day.
This tracks all the words you understand while reading, including status 4-Learned words and ✓-Known words.

"When you start you have 0 Known Words. As you use LingQ, the system learns which words you know. With prior knowledge, your known words can increase quickly. If you are starting from scratch, your Known Words count will grow slowly at first. That’s okay! Over time, through lots of reading and reviewing, you will learn your first words. Words used frequently will stick first. And then your rate of learning words will gradually increase. When you know a word, hit the checkmark. Or, when you turn a page, the blue words you didn’t look up will be marked as known automatically. If you don’t know a word, don’t worry. You can always just click on it and save it."
Read, listen, create LingQs and watch your Known Words count grow.
How this will change for you
"This tracks how many words you've saved translations for."

"The more LingQs you create, the wider your exposure to the written language. And thus the better your chances of learning more words. Don't waste your time deciding which words to LingQ and which to ignore. Just LingQ every word you don't know. Important words will resurface in subsequent lessons. And over time you will learn them naturally."

"In a completely new language, you should LingQ every word you encounter, since you don't yet know any words. As you progress, you will find you already know some of the new words you encounter. But your rate of creating LingQs should stay relatively constant. You should be reading more and, thus, still encountering new words all the time."
Create lots of LingQs to learn lots of words.
How your lingqs learned will change
LingQs Learned is the subset of Known Words which were previously saved as LingQs.

"Like Known Words, LingQs Learned will lag behind other metrics if you are a novice in the language. However, through extensive exposure, you will reach a stage where LingQs Learned grows rapidly and with it your understanding of the language. With pre-existing knowledge in a language, your Known Words count will grow quickly at first. So LingQs Learned is a better measure for the progress you are making in the language. It measures how many words you’ve learned from your activity on LingQ. You can increase the status of LingQs manually. And the status of a LingQ will automatically increase by 1 if you get the word correct twice within a single review session."
Gets lots of exposure. Be patient and your LingQs Learned will grow like a snowball rolling down a hill.
This tracks the time you spend listening to lesson audio.

"By immersing yourself in native audio, you will come to recognize the natural flow of the language, improve pronunciation, intonation and overall speaking fluency. You can't control when your listening comprehension reaches a level at which you can understand native speakers at ease, but you can control how much time you spend listening to the language."

"Just get a lot of exposure, so your brain starts to become familiar with the sounds of the language. Your understanding will improve over time. Listen to your Playlist throughout the day whenever you can. On your commute, while doing dishes, at the gym, etc. Repeat listening is important, especially at the beginning to familiarize yourself with the sounds and reinforce vocabulary & grammar patterns that you were exposed to in reading. But make sure to regularly listen to new lessons too. A balance of repetition and novelty is crucial."
"At first, you won't understand what you hear. That's okay."
This tracks the number of words you read in your target language.

Your brain loves context. By reading you learn words in the context of meaningful content. Not only will you build your vocabulary by reading, but you will grow an intuitive understanding of grammatical patterns as well. Extensive reading exposes you to authentic language usage, which is crucial for improving fluency.

"That's okay. Look up the words you don't know and create LingQs. Over time, your understanding will improve. Start with a small amount of content at an easier level. Resist the urge to stay on the same lesson until you understand everything. Move on to new lessons regularly so you get a wider exposure to the language. Come back and re-read past lessons occasionally. And before long, you will be moving on to more difficult and more interesting content. Remember that consuming content of interest keeps you engaged with the language so you will learn more."
Reading is the most powerful way to learn lots of words.
"When first getting started, you won't understand what you read."
As you read more, your vocabulary and language proficiency will naturally improve.
How Your Reading Speed Will Change
This tracks how many words per minute you read in your lessons.
Reading speed is a strong indication of how comfortable you are in the language. The quicker you read, the faster your brain processes the language.

When you get started with a new language, your reading speed will be quite slow. As you progress, your speed should increase. Of course, you should then challenge yourself with increasingly complex material, which will contribute to lowering your reading speed. But overtime, you will likely see your reading speed increase - which is a strong indicator of progress.
Read a lot and watch your reading speed accelerate.
How this will change for you
This tracks the time spent in conversations with **link**tutors**link** booked on the LingQ web platform.
"Most of us are learning a language to speak the language. So eventually, it's important to be speaking in your new language on a regular basis."

"We don't expect new learners to start speaking until they reach Beginner 2 level in the language. However, if you want to practice speaking, you can use the speaking activity in sentence reviews, or head over to book a tutor conversation. Independent research has found that reading and listening on LingQ improves speaking ability. Like most skills, when you first get started, it's going to be awkward and clumsy. That's okay. With more practice, you will improve. Have fun with it. You're never going to be “ready.” But eventually, you need to just get started. Focus on communicating, rather than trying to perform."
"If you're here to learn to speak, you don't have to do it immediately, but you do eventually need to start speaking regularly."
At this level, we recommend introducing speaking into your learning goals.
How Your Study Time Will Change
This tracks all the time you spend reading, listening & reviewing LingQs.

"Progress in language learning is largely a function of how much time you spend with the language. You can't control when the language will become familiar, understandable or usable. However, you can control how much time you spend learning the language."

As you acquire more of the language, direct your learning toward content that is more interesting to you. This will keep you motivated to spend more and more time with the language, which in turn will help accelerate your learning.
Try to maintain a regular habit of learning at least a little bit every day.
Spend a lot of time with your new language.
How this will change for you

"Writing is a pressure-free opportunity to practice expressing yourself in the language. It's a great stepping-stone to speaking and an opportunity to improve your accuracy in the language."
"We don't expect new learners to start writing until they reach Beginner 2 level in the language: however, if you want to practice writing, go to the **link**Writing Exchange**link**."
"At first, you won't understand what you hear. That's okay."
After you’ve done a fair bit of reading and listening, start writing to practice expressing yourself in your new language.
